## Exact correction and consumer resolution

`selection.rs` now declares `#[path = "read_worker.rs"] pub(super) mod read_worker` exactly once. No read_worker declaration exists in windows_runtime_v201 root, UIA secure or Word focus. Native Word uses `super::read_worker`; Word focus uses `super::super::read_worker`, which both resolve to selection regardless of whether selection is a child of runtime, failure binary or browser-test parent. UIA secure uses its sibling `super::selection::read_worker`; pub(super) visibility allows that parent-level sibling access. The previous requirement for a binary-root read_worker is eliminated.

The prior stored worker diff is exclusively that common declaration/reference wiring, plus replacing the explicit complex channel pair type with `mpsc::sync_channel::<Read<Q,R>>(1)` and dropping unused Receiver import. Active runtime v201 is byte-identical to the approved stored worker. All metadata/security checks, native mutation/Undo/uncertain latch, single AtomicU8 Ready/Busy/Quarantined protocol and portable/Windows tests remain unchanged. Sharing the generic module does not merge the separate UIA secure and Word focus READER statics; each still owns its independently bounded read-only worker.

The original cycle 2 report found root-relative module resolution would fail for the directly imported standalone selection consumer. The selection-owned declaration fixes this concrete issue without another product file or root-specific adaptation. Parent also reports verification of standalone/browser-test parent hierarchies; this targeted review establishes the source paths statically, without compilation.

Parent reports prior CI37764117791 passed five reader tests, library tests and Windows compilation before Clippy rejected duplicate module/type complexity. Those results are historical evidence for the old wiring, not a new CI success claim. All prior no-hard-total-timeout and actual-Word acceptance limits remain.

Compared every current file directly with FILES decoded from the prior worker base64 in `launch-worker-readback.json`, following corrected requirements PASS. The complete delta is one selection-owned reader declaration, its three relative uses, and channel type-inference simplification/removal of Receiver import. Runtime v201 is byte-identical. No reader state-machine, tests, fresh metadata, native mutation, Undo or uncertainty logic changed.

`selection::read_worker` is declared `pub(super)` once. Word native resolves its sibling through `super::read_worker`; Word focus resolves the selection sibling through `super::super::read_worker`. These references depend on selection ownership, which remains valid for runtime and directly imported standalone selection consumers. UIA secure is a sibling of selection and resolves through `super::selection::read_worker`; pub(super) permits access from that parent and descendants. No crate-root reader declaration is needed. The separate security/focus READER statics remain separate provider owners; sharing the generic implementation does not share admission state or positive observations.

`mpsc::sync_channel::<Read<Q,R>>(1)` provides the same queue/request/result types as the removed explicit pair annotation. The worker closure infers Receiver<Read<Q,R>>, preserving ownership, one-worker admission, Ready/Busy/Quarantined protocol and late-result refusal. It removes the reported complex type without weakening a bound.

Read-only exact diff, decoded Python AST extraction and SHA-256 verification only. No execution, compiler/test run, CI launch, commit or remote mutation. Parent-reported prior CI37764117791 test/compile successes precede this wiring change and do not establish fresh CI success. Carry forward prior source quality approval and its limits: NativeOM may still block, sent callbacks are not an absolute timeout guarantee, and actual installed Word hang/formatting/Undo acceptance remains pending.
